spec_match.rationale: The six flex patterns use real column-rule/row-rule-in-flex declarations, but the calendar block titles itself 'repeat syntax' while actually using plain comma lists (row-rule-width: 2px, 1px), and whether that list form matches the shipped css-gaps-1 subset is unverified.

interactive.rationale: The only interaction is the generated 'scenario focus' panel, which highlights and summarises blocks — it never changes any rule's rendered output, so the feature itself is a static showcase (below invariant 7's toggle/slider minimum) (assessed from code review and the rendered DOM; the controls were not driven in this session).

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises 'alternating rule styles with the repeat() syntax', but no repeat() appears anywhere on the page.

edge_cases.rationale: The note honestly states Chrome 149+ and that layouts degrade to no separators (true here), but there is no live detection, and alternating-list behaviour at wrap boundaries is not explored.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite covers the real surface and honestly fails 6 of 8 in this browser.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Cloud-fallback observation only, NOT browser-verified per auto-research.md §0 — headless Chromium 141 (full-page screenshot + DOM, not chrome-devtools-mcp): all six patterns render their content with no rules (expected here), the walkthrough panel built six buttons, conformance panel 2/6/0; walkthrough clicks were not driven. chrome-devtools-mcp is unavailable in this cloud session (the auto-research.md section-0 blocker applies, so this is NOT browser verification): what was exercised is page load, full-page screenshot read, served/dumped DOM state and the /conformance/ route result; driving every control and capturing console/network evidence remains for an MCP-equipped session.

design_system.rationale: Variables throughout; walkthrough buttons set background and color together; snippets scroll horizontally.

accessibility.rationale: The walkthrough output is aria-live and buttons are native, but five of its six generated buttons are identically labelled 'demo block' (screenshot evidence), making them useless to screen-reader and sighted users alike; rules themselves are decorative so their absence needs no announcement.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Patterns wrap and snippets scroll; clean at 1280px headless, ≈360px untested.

openQuestions.title: Use (or drop) repeat() — the page and blurb promise it but never use it
openQuestions.detail: Demo 6 is titled 'alternating row-rule (repeat syntax)' and the index card sells repeat(), yet the CSS uses plain comma lists. Verify the shipped css-gaps-1 grammar (rule-builder exercised real repeat() syntax), then either demonstrate actual repeat(auto, …)/repeat(N, …) alternation in the calendar block or retitle it 'comma list'.

openQuestions.title: Add one interactive control that changes a rule
openQuestions.detail: Every pattern is static. A single style/width/colour control applied to the focused pattern (reusing the walkthrough's selection) — or per-block toggles like data-table-rules has — would meet invariant 7's hands-on minimum and let users see rules appear/disappear in supporting browsers.

openQuestions.title: Fix the walkthrough's duplicate 'demo block' button labels
openQuestions.detail: labelFor() falls back to the first class name, so five buttons all read 'demo block'. Use each block's .demo-block-title text (e.g. 'Horizontal navigation', 'Breadcrumbs') so the scenario buttons are distinguishable visually and to assistive tech.

openQuestions.title: Detect support live
openQuestions.detail: Pair the static Chrome 149+ note with a CSS.supports('row-rule-color','red') probe that switches the note to an explicit 'separators not rendered in this browser' state, matching the honest-capability rule.

summary: Reviewed with the headless-Chromium-141 cloud fallback (not chrome-devtools-mcp): full-page screenshot + DOM of /v149/css-gap-decorations/flex-dividers/ and the feature /conformance/ route (HTTP 200; panel 2 pass / 6 fail / 0 blocked). Six well-chosen flex patterns with honest degrade copy and correct references, but the page is effectively static (the walkthrough only highlights blocks), the advertised repeat() syntax never appears, and the generated scenario buttons collapse into five identical 'demo block' labels. Rules do not render in this browser, as the note predicts; interactions were not driven headless.
